decision: Ordinary captures and closure copies own independent private state; sharing is explicit.
behavior: Closure literals snapshot unlisted enclosing locals; [@name]() explicitly captures a shared local cell.
Plain copies of private counters return 1, 1; explicit shared counters return 1, 2.
Parameters, returns, recursive containers and nested closures preserve private value copies.
Const callable invocations use temporary private copies; captured const locals remain read-only.
Value-returning dictionary getters return private copies. An @ callback parameter can update @counters[key].
Module globals keep their identity. Implementation-language .jo closures keep their lexical sharing behavior.

validation.standalone_artifacts: All four dewy-core host downloads uploaded successfully.

local_selections.purpose: Affected arithmetic, bounds, callback, collection and closure regression migration.
Closure, formatting, watch and shared-core checks after an independent C bootstrap; before the stable-call optimization.
Closures, argument evaluation, shared core and prompt behavior after the stable-call optimization.
Dictionary copies, mutable entries and callback argument regression checks.

validation.scope: The extra native hosts execute a smoke selection, not every Linux or graphics-driver check.

performance.protocol: Five alternating fresh-process samples after one warmup per compiler/workload/mode; one emission worker. All counter results checked.
performance.initial_pin_regression: Always pinning the called environment raised ten-million-call CPU medians from roughly 27–31 ms to 86–101 ms.
performance.interpretation: The stable-call path removes the counter regression. Self-build CPU time is essentially unchanged, and Netpong compilation costs about 3% more in this pilot. Wall measurements are noisy; no broad runtime speedup is claimed.
performance.later_change: The subsequent dictionary fix preserves the @ syntax marker during AST rewriting; it was tested but the performance pilot was not repeated for it.

remaining_limits: Arrays that can contain functions eagerly copy their elements and private environments. Ordinary data arrays retain COW; immutable private closure environments can share storage.
Shared captures currently name enclosing local bindings, not arbitrary places or escaping mutable parameters.
Shared cells that can contain functions are rejected conservatively to prevent reference cycles.
Dewy partial-application syntax remains unsupported; use a closure wrapper.
